``````text
//! Static logical work of successful segments (C3).
//!
//! The evaluator charges one unit per statement dispatch and one per distinct
//! expression node it visits. Its cache is per statement, and `And`/`Or`
//! evaluate both operands, so a successful statement costs exactly
//! `1 + |nodes reachable from its root expression|`, independent of values.
//! Segment j runs from entry site j (0 = start) and stops at the next await,
//! whose entry charge of 1 is paid but whose guard belongs to segment j+1.
use super::{ActionPlan, StageLogical, StagePlan};
use crate::policy::{Cost, Meter};
use crate::{Error, Expr, ExprId, Program, Statement, UInt};

fn overflow() -> Error {
    Error::new("bound", "Stage logical plan exceeds u128.")
}

fn add(a: UInt, b: UInt) -> Result<UInt, Error> {
    a.0.checked_add(b.0).map(UInt).ok_or_else(overflow)
}

/// Distinct expression nodes reachable from `root`: the per-statement cache
/// charges each shared DAG node once.
fn expression_nodes(program: &Program, root: ExprId) -> Result<u128, Error> {
    let mut seen = vec![false; program.expressions.len()];
    let mut pending = vec![root];
    let mut count = 0_u128;
    while let Some(id) = pending.pop() {
        let index = usize::from(id);
        let node = program
            .expressions
            .get(index)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::new("expression", "Expression index out of bounds."))?;
        if std::mem::replace(&mut seen[index], true) {
            continue;
        }
        count += 1;
        match node {
            Expr::Binary { lhs, rhs, .. } => pending.extend([*lhs, *rhs]),
            Expr::Not { value } => pending.push(*value),
            Expr::LiabilityPresent { .. }
            | Expr::LiabilityAmount { .. }
            | Expr::Literal { .. }
            | Expr::Name { .. } => {}
        }
    }
    Ok(count)
}

fn root(statement: &Statement) -> ExprId {
    match statement {
        Statement::Await { guard, .. } => *guard,
        Statement::Let { value, .. }
        | Statement::Next { value, .. }
        | Statement::Emit { value, .. } => *value,
        Statement::Requires { predicate } | Statement::Ensures { predicate } => *predicate,
        Statement::Transfer { amount, .. }
        | Statement::Fee { amount, .. }
        | Statement::Liability { amount, .. }
        | Statement::Discharge { amount, .. } => *amount,
    }
}

/// Successful cost of one statement. For an Await this is its resume dispatch
/// plus guard; reaching an Await at segment exit costs 1 instead.
pub(crate) fn statement_cost(program: &Program, statement: &Statement) -> Result<UInt, Error> {
    let nodes = expression_nodes(program, root(statement))?;
    nodes.checked_add(1).map(UInt).ok_or_else(overflow)
}

fn segment_cost(
    program: &Program,
    action: usize,
    plan: &ActionPlan,
    segment: usize,
) -> Result<UInt, Error> {
    let statements = &program
        .actions
        .get(action)
        .ok_or_else(|| Error::new("program", "Stage plan invariant violated: action."))?
        .statements;
    let ordinal = |site: usize| -> Result<usize, Error> {
        plan.sites
            .get(site - 1)
            .map(|s| usize::from(s.ordinal))
            .filter(|ordinal| *ordinal < statements.len())
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::new("program", "Stage plan invariant violated: site."))
    };
    let n = plan.sites.len();
    let begin = if segment == 0 { 0 } else { ordinal(segment)? };
    let end = if segment == n {
        statements.len()
    } else {
        ordinal(segment + 1)?
    };
    if begin >= end && !(segment == 0 && begin == end) {
        return Err(Error::new(
            "program",
            "Stage plan invariant violated: ordinals.",
        ));
    }
    let mut total = UInt(0);
    for (offset, statement) in statements[begin..end].iter().enumerate() {
        // Only an advance's first statement is an Await (its dispatch).
        if matches!(statement, Statement::Await { .. }) && (segment == 0 || offset != 0) {
            return Err(Error::new(
                "program",
                "Stage plan invariant violated: unplanned await.",
            ));
        }
        total = add(total, statement_cost(program, statement)?)?;
    }
    if segment < n {
        total = add(total, UInt(1))?;
    }
    Ok(total)
}

/// Fills `segment_cost`, `committed_before` and `plan_total` for every action
/// of a Sol-built plan whose cost vectors are still empty.
pub(crate) fn fill(program: &Program, plan: &mut StagePlan) -> Result<(), Error> {
    if plan.actions.len() != program.actions.len() {
        return Err(Error::new(
            "program",
            "Stage plan invariant violated: action count.",
        ));
    }
    for (index, action) in plan.actions.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        if !action.segment_cost.is_empty()
            || !action.committed_before.is_empty()
            || action.plan_total != UInt(0)
        {
            return Err(Error::new(
                "program",
                "Stage plan invariant violated: costs are already filled.",
            ));
        }
        let mut costs = Vec::with_capacity(action.sites.len() + 1);
        let mut committed = Vec::with_capacity(action.sites.len() + 1);
        let mut total = UInt(0);
        for segment in 0..=action.sites.len() {
            let cost = segment_cost(program, index, action, segment)?;
            committed.push(total);
            total = add(total, cost)?;
            costs.push(cost);
        }
        action.segment_cost = costs;
        action.committed_before = committed;
        action.plan_total = total;
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Attempted work of a resume whose guard at `site` is false: one dispatch
/// plus the guard's distinct nodes. Committed work is unchanged by it.
pub(crate) fn dispatch_cost(
    program: &Program,
    plan: &ActionPlan,
    site: u16,
) -> Result<UInt, Error> {
    let action = program
        .actions
        .iter()
        .find(|a| a.name == plan.action)
        .ok_or_else(|| Error::new("stage_site", "Unknown staged action."))?;
    let statement = usize::from(site)
        .checked_sub(1)
        .and_then(|i| plan.sites.get(i))
        .and_then(|s| action.statements.get(usize::from(s.ordinal)))
        .filter(|s| matches!(s, Statement::Await { .. }))
        .ok_or_else(|| Error::new("stage_site", "Pending site is not an await of this action."))?;
    statement_cost(program, statement)
}

/// Start refusal before evaluation (C3). Without a cap there is no admission
/// check. Returns the meter limit of segment 0.
pub(crate) fn start_preflight(plan: &ActionPlan, cap: Option<UInt>) -> Result<UInt, Error> {
    let first = *plan
        .segment_cost
        .first()
        .ok_or_else(|| Error::new("stage_logical", "Stage plan has no segment costs."))?;
    if let Some(cap) = cap
        && plan.plan_total > cap
    {
        return Err(Error::new(
            "stage_logical",
            "Action plan total exceeds the logical cap.",
        ));
    }
    Ok(first)
}

/// R6. Call only after R1-R5 admitted `site`. The CLI cap checks this
/// invocation only and can never raise the stored cap, which the output
/// continuation carries unchanged. Returns the meter limit of segment `site`.
pub(crate) fn resume_preflight(
    plan: &ActionPlan,
    site: u16,
    logical: &StageLogical,
    cli_cap: Option<UInt>,
) -> Result<UInt, Error> {
    let refuse = |message: &str| Error::new("stage_logical", message);
    let index = usize::from(site);
    let (Some(before), Some(cost)) = (
        plan.committed_before.get(index),
        plan.segment_cost.get(index),
    ) else {
        return Err(refuse("Pending site has no planned segment."));
    };
    if index == 0 || logical.committed != *before {
        return Err(refuse("Committed work differs from the stage plan."));
    }
    let needed = logical
        .committed
        .0
        .checked_add(cost.0)
        .ok_or_else(|| refuse("Committed work overflows u128."))?;
    let effective = match (cli_cap, logical.cap) {
        (Some(cli), Some(stored)) if cli > stored => {
            return Err(refuse("Logical cap cannot exceed the stored cap."));
        }
        (Some(cli), _) => Some(cli),
        (None, stored) => stored,
    };
    if effective.is_some_and(|cap| needed > cap.0) {
        return Err(refuse("Next segment exceeds the logical cap."));
    }
    Ok(*cost)
}

pub(crate) fn segment_meter(limit: UInt) -> Meter {
    Meter::new(Cost {
        logical: limit,
        ..Cost::default()
    })
}

/// H26: the evaluator must have charged exactly the planned work.
pub(crate) fn require_static(meter: &Meter, expected: UInt) -> Result<(), Error> {
    if meter.used().logical != expected {
        return Err(Error::new("stage_logical", "static cost premise violated"));
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Committed work after segment `segment` succeeds.
pub(crate) fn committed_after(plan: &ActionPlan, segment: usize) -> Result<UInt, Error> {
    match (
        plan.committed_before.get(segment),
        plan.segment_cost.get(segment),
    ) {
        (Some(before), Some(cost)) => add(*before, *cost),
        _ => Err(Error::new(
            "stage_logical",
            "Segment is absent from the stage plan.",
        )),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]

            "mori::core::stage_logical"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn h26_require_static_rejects_any_meter_difference() {
        let mut meter = segment_meter(UInt(6));
        for _ in 0..5 {
            meter.charge(CostPlane::Logical, UInt(1)).unwrap();
        }
        let error = require_static(&meter, UInt(6)).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(error.code, "mori::core::stage_logical");
        assert_eq!(error.message, "static cost premise violated");
        meter.charge(CostPlane::Logical, UInt(1)).unwrap();
        assert!(require_static(&meter, UInt(6)).is_ok());
        assert!(require_static(&meter, UInt(5)).is_err());
        // The planned limit is a hard ceiling: excess work cannot be metered.
        assert!(meter.charge(CostPlane::Logical, UInt(1)).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn committed_after_is_checked_prefix_plus_segment() {
        let p = plan(&[11, 15, 10]);
        assert_eq!(committed_after(&p, 0).unwrap(), UInt(11));
        assert_eq!(committed_after(&p, 1).unwrap(), UInt(26));
        assert_eq!(committed_after(&p, 2).unwrap(), UInt(36));
        assert!(committed_after(&p, 3).is_err());
        let huge = ActionPlan {
            committed_before: vec![UInt(0), UInt(u128::MAX)],
            ..plan(&[u128::MAX, 1])
        };
        assert_eq!(
            committed_after(&huge, 1).unwrap_err().code,
            "mori::core::bound"
        );
    }
}
``````

``````text
//! Strict bounded decoding of local stage files and the R7 canonical boundary.
//!
//! Size limits apply to bytes actually read, before parsing. Parsing keeps the
//! legacy duplicate-key, depth and node limits; only the byte ceiling differs.
//! A resumed boundary is checked as written and is never re-sorted.
use super::{Continuation, NamedValue, StageEvent, StagedProgram};
use crate::{AssetId, Error, MAX_TRACE_CELLS, Program, Snapshot, Statement};
use serde::de::DeserializeOwned;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::path::Path;

pub use super::{MAX_CONTINUATION_BYTES, MAX_EVENT_BYTES};

pub const CONTINUATION_TOO_LARGE: &str = "Continuation JSON exceeds 4 MiB";
pub const EVENT_TOO_LARGE: &str = "Stage event JSON exceeds 64 KiB";

/// Reads at most `max + 1` bytes, so the limit holds even if the file grows
/// after it is opened. Oversized or non-UTF-8 input fails with `json`.
pub fn read_bounded(path: &Path, max: usize, too_large: &'static str) -> Result<String, Error> {
    use std::io::Read;
    let file = std::fs::File::open(path)
        .map_err(|e| Error::new("io", format!("Cannot open stage input: {e}")))?;
    let limit = u64::try_from(max).unwrap_or(u64::MAX).saturating_add(1);
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
    file.take(limit)
        .read_to_end(&mut bytes)
        .map_err(|e| Error::new("io", format!("Cannot read stage input: {e}")))?;
    if bytes.len() > max {
        return Err(Error::new("json", too_large));
    }
    String::from_utf8(bytes).map_err(|_| Error::new("json", "Stage input is not UTF-8"))
}

fn strict<T: DeserializeOwned>(
    text: &str,
    max: usize,
    too_large: &'static str,
) -> Result<T, Error> {
    let value = crate::json::parse_limited(text, max, too_large)?;
    serde_json::from_value(value).map_err(|e| Error::new("json", e.to_string()))
}

/// Exactly one `Continuation`; unknown fields, a missing `cap` key and
/// non-canonical UInt strings are rejected by the type's derives.
pub fn continuation(text: &str) -> Result<Continuation, Error> {
    strict(text, MAX_CONTINUATION_BYTES, CONTINUATION_TOO_LARGE)
}

pub fn event(text: &str) -> Result<StageEvent, Error> {
    strict(text, MAX_EVENT_BYTES, EVENT_TOO_LARGE)
}

type Identity<'a> = (&'a AssetId, &'a str, &'a str);

/// Source-fixed liability identities over every action of the program.
fn registry(p: &Program) -> Result<BTreeMap<&str, Identity<'_>>, Error> {
    let mut identities = BTreeMap::new();
    for stmt in p.actions.iter().flat_map(|action| &action.statements) {
        if let Statement::Liability {
            name,
            asset,
            debtor,
            creditor,
            ..
        } = stmt
        {
            let id = asset_identity(p, asset)?;
            let identity = (id, debtor.as_str(), creditor.as_str());
            if identities
                .insert(name.as_str(), identity)
                .is_some_and(|existing| existing != identity)
            {
                return Err(Error::new(
                    "liability",
                    format!("Conflicting source liability identity for {name:?}."),
                ));
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(identities)
}

fn asset_identity<'a>(p: &'a Program, name: &str) -> Result<&'a AssetId, Error> {
    p.assets
        .iter()
        .find(|a| a.name == name)
        .map(|a| &a.identity)
        .ok_or_else(|| Error::new("asset", format!("Unknown asset {name:?}.")))
}

/// R7: the legacy `scenario_snapshot` predicates applied to a resumed boundary
/// without normalisation. Codes and messages follow `scenario_snapshot`;
/// ordering failures are new `balance`/`liability` messages.
///
/// Balances keep the baseline predicate: every account the whole action
/// transfers from or to must be present, and other declared-asset accounts
/// (such as an untouched observer) are preserved, not refused.
pub fn canonical_boundary(
    sp: &StagedProgram,
    action: usize,
    captures: &[NamedValue],
    b: &Snapshot,
) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let p = sp.program();
    let (Some(a), Some(plan)) = (p.actions.get(action), sp.plan().actions.get(action)) else {
        return Err(Error::new("stage_site", "Unknown staged action."));
    };
    // (d) Snapshot has no inputs component (U-1); R4 alone binds captures.
    let _ = captures;
    if b.balances.len() > 4096 || b.liabilities.len() > 1024 {
        return Err(Error::new(
            "bound",
            "Scenario exceeds 4,096 balances or 1,024 liabilities.",
        ));
    }
    // (a) States: exactly the declared states, each of its declared type.
    if b.state.len() != p.states.len() {
        return Err(Error::new(
            "state",
            "Boundary must provide every declared state value and no other.",
        ));
    }
    for d in &p.states {
        let value = b
            .state
            .get(&d.name)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::new("state", format!("Missing state {:?}.", d.name)))?;
        if value.ty() != d.ty {
            return Err(Error::new(
                "state",
                format!("Wrong type for state {:?}.", d.name),
            ));
        }
    }
    // (b) Balances: declared assets, valid accounts, strictly ascending by
    // (asset, account), which also excludes duplicates.
    let ids: BTreeSet<&AssetId> = p.assets.iter().map(|a| &a.identity).collect();
    let mut previous: Option<(&AssetId, &str)> = None;
    for balance in &b.balances {
        if !ids.contains(&balance.asset) {
            return Err(Error::new(
                "asset",
                format!(
                    "Undeclared exact asset identity for account {:?}.",
                    balance.account
                ),
            ));
        }
        if balance.account.is_empty() || balance.account.len() > 1024 {
            return Err(Error::new(
                "balance",
                "Duplicate or invalid balance account/asset.",
            ));
        }
        let key = (&balance.asset, balance.account.as_str());
        if previous.is_some_and(|prior| prior >= key) {
            return Err(Error::new("balance", "Balances are not canonical"));
        }
        previous = Some(key);
    }
    for stmt in &a.statements {
        if let Statement::Transfer {
            asset, from, to, ..
        }
        | Statement::Fee {
            asset, from, to, ..
        } = stmt
        {
            let id = asset_identity(p, asset)?;
            for account in [from, to] {
                if b.balances
                    .binary_search_by(|x| {
                        (&x.asset, x.account.as_str()).cmp(&(id, account.as_str()))
                    })
                    .is_err()
                {
                    return Err(Error::new(
                        "balance",
                        format!("Missing explicit balance for {account:?} and asset {asset:?}."),
                    ));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    // (c) Liabilities: strictly ascending by name; every name is a source
    // liability of this program with exactly its registered identity.
    let registry = registry(p)?;
    let mut previous: Option<&str> = None;
    for l in &b.liabilities {
        if !ids.contains(&l.asset) {
            return Err(Error::new(
                "asset",
                "Liability uses undeclared exact asset identity.",
            ));
        }
        if l.name.is_empty()
            || l.name.len() > 1024
            || l.debtor.is_empty()
            || l.creditor.is_empty()
            || l.debtor.len() > 1024
            || l.creditor.len() > 1024
        {
            return Err(Error::new(
                "liability",
                "Invalid or duplicate liability identity.",
            ));
        }
        if previous.is_some_and(|prior| prior >= l.name.as_str()) {
            return Err(Error::new("liability", "Liabilities are not canonical"));
        }
        previous = Some(l.name.as_str());
        if registry.get(l.name.as_str())
            != Some(&(&l.asset, l.debtor.as_str(), l.creditor.as_str()))
        {
            return Err(Error::new(
                "liability",
                format!("Existing liability identity differs for {:?}.", l.name),
            ));
        }
    }
    // (e) Trace cells over the whole action, as at start.
    let added = a
        .statements
        .iter()
        .filter(|stmt| matches!(stmt, Statement::Liability { .. }))
        .count();
    let records = p.states.len() + b.balances.len() + b.liabilities.len() + added + 1;
    if records.saturating_mul(usize::from(plan.statement_count) + 2) > MAX_TRACE_CELLS {
        return Err(Error::new(
            "bound",
            "Scenario and action exceed 65,536 trace snapshot records.",
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}
``````

``````text
//! Canonical program and plan digests. Both hash `intent::canonical`, the
//! same encoding the backend uses for its `/3` program hash.
use super::StagePlan;
use crate::{Error, Program};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

fn digest<T: serde::Serialize>(value: &T) -> Result<[u8; 32], Error> {
    Ok(Sha256::digest(crate::intent::canonical(value)?).into())
}

pub(crate) fn hex(hash: &[u8; 32]) -> String {
    crate::intent::hex(hash)
}

/// Exact comparison against the canonical 64-character lowercase encoding.
pub(crate) fn matches(text: &str, hash: &[u8; 32]) -> bool {
    text == hex(hash)
}

pub(crate) fn program_hash(program: &Program) -> Result<[u8; 32], Error> {
    digest(program)
}

/// Hashes the costed plan, which already names its program hash and format.
pub(crate) fn plan_hash(plan: &StagePlan) -> Result<[u8; 32], Error> {
    let filled = plan.program_hash.len() == 64
        && plan
            .program_hash
            .bytes()
            .all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit() || (b'a'..=b'f').contains(&b));
    if !filled {
        return Err(Error::new(
            "program",
            "Stage plan invariant violated: program hash is not filled.",
        ));
    }
    digest(plan)
}
``````

``````text
//! Staged `moriarty/2` programs and their local continuation interface.
//!
//! Local and unsigned only. Event binders and captures are caller-chosen values
//! (no authentication), a continuation can be resumed any number of times (no
//! consumption tracking), and no stage authority exists. Outputs carry
//! `STAGE_LABELS` so these limits stay visible.
mod admit;
mod cost;
pub mod decode;
mod digest;
#[cfg(feature = "core2-disjoint-draft")]
pub mod disjoint;
mod plan;
mod profile;
mod report;
mod validate;

pub use crate::LOGICAL_COST_PROFILE_2;
pub use admit::{resume, start};
pub use plan::{ActionPlan, AwaitSite, CaptureSlot, Origin, StageBinder, StagePlan};
pub use profile::{require_core1, require_core2};
pub use report::outcome_report;

use crate::{Error, Execution, Liability, Program, Snapshot, UInt, Value};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

pub const LANGUAGE_2: &str = "moriarty/2";
pub const SEMANTICS_2: &str = "moriarty-core/2";
pub const STAGE_PLAN_FORMAT: &str = "moriarty-stage-plan/1";
pub const CONTINUATION_FORMAT: &str = "moriarty-continuation/1";
pub const STAGE_EVENT_FORMAT: &str = "moriarty-stage-event/1";
pub const MAX_AWAITS_PER_ACTION: usize = 16;
pub const MAX_EVENT_BINDERS: usize = 16;
pub const MAX_CAPTURE_SLOTS: usize = 256;
pub const MAX_CONTINUATION_BYTES: usize = 4 * 1_048_576;
pub const MAX_EVENT_BYTES: usize = 65_536;
/// Inserted verbatim into every `/2` output object.
pub const STAGE_LABELS: [(&str, &str); 3] = [
    ("qualification", "local-reference-stage"),
    ("authentication", "none"),
    ("consumption", "untracked"),
];

/// A `/2` program that passed profile, validation, plan invariants and static
/// costing, with its canonical digests. Only `load` constructs one; there is
/// no public constructor, `Default` or `Deserialize`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct StagedProgram {
    program: Program,
    plan: StagePlan,
    program_hash: [u8; 32],
    plan_hash: [u8; 32],
}
impl StagedProgram {
    pub fn program(&self) -> &Program {
        &self.program
    }
    pub fn plan(&self) -> &StagePlan {
        &self.plan
    }
    pub fn program_hash(&self) -> [u8; 32] {
        self.program_hash
    }
    pub fn plan_hash(&self) -> [u8; 32] {
        self.plan_hash
    }
    /// Declaration index of an action; plan and program actions share it.
    pub(crate) fn action_index(&self, name: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        self.program.actions.iter().position(|a| a.name == name)
    }
}

/// Parses, admits and plans a `moriarty/2` source. Legacy `parse`/`validate`
/// remain `/1`-only, so a `/2` source fails every legacy consumer.
pub fn load(src: &str) -> Result<StagedProgram, Error> {
    let program = crate::parser::parse_v2(src)?;
    profile::require_core2(&program)?;
    validate::validate_v2(&program)?;
    let mut plan = plan::build(&program)?;
    validate::plan_invariants(&program, &plan)?;
    cost::fill(&program, &mut plan)?;
    validate::cost_invariants(&program, &plan)?;
    let program_hash = digest::program_hash(&program)?;
    plan.program_hash = digest::hex(&program_hash);
    let plan_hash = digest::plan_hash(&plan)?;
    Ok(StagedProgram {
        program,
        plan,
        program_hash,
        plan_hash,
    })
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct NamedValue {
    pub name: String,
    pub value: Value,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct StageLogical {
    pub profile: String,
    /// Mandatory key; `None` is written as `null`.
    #[serde(deserialize_with = "Option::deserialize")]
    pub cap: Option<UInt>,
    pub committed: UInt,
}
/// Resume input. `site` and `captures` are the executing action's pending
/// frame; `boundary` is the legacy Snapshot. Nothing here is authenticated.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Continuation {
    pub format: String,
    pub program_hash: String,
    pub plan_hash: String,
    pub action: String,
    pub site: u16,
    pub captures: Vec<NamedValue>,
    pub logical: StageLogical,
    pub boundary: Snapshot,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct StageEvent {
    pub format: String,
    pub action: String,
    pub label: String,
    pub values: Vec<NamedValue>,
}
/// Local frame of one action. `site == 0` exactly when `captures` is empty
/// and the action is idle; no padding is represented locally.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct PendingFrame {
    pub site: u16,
    pub captures: Vec<NamedValue>,
}
impl PendingFrame {
    pub(crate) fn idle() -> Self {
        Self {
            site: 0,
            captures: Vec::new(),
        }
    }
}
/// Output only. Segment history is never decoded or trusted on resume, so no
/// `Deserialize` exists over the shared Await-bearing `Statement`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct StageSegment {
    pub action: String,
    pub frame_pre: PendingFrame,
    pub frame_post: PendingFrame,
    pub execution: Execution,
}
/// `residual` lists every post-boundary liability with a positive amount, in
/// the existing complete `Liability` representation.
// Public outcome; boxing `Waiting` would change every caller's pattern.
#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub enum StageOutcome {
    Waiting {
        advanced: bool,
        segment: Option<StageSegment>,
        continuation: Continuation,
        attempted: UInt,
        residual: Vec<Liability>,
    },
    Complete {
        segment: StageSegment,
        committed: UInt,
        attempted: UInt,
        residual: Vec<Liability>,
    },
}
/// A rejected invocation publishes no segment, effects or continuation.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, thiserror::Error)]
#[error("{error}")]
pub struct StageRejection {
    pub error: Error,
    pub attempted: UInt,
    pub committed: UInt,
}

/// Positive residual duties of a boundary, in its (name-sorted) order.
pub(crate) fn residual(snapshot: &Snapshot) -> Vec<Liability> {
    snapshot
        .liabilities
        .iter()
        .filter(|l| l.amount.0 > 0)
        .cloned()
        .collect()
}
``````

``````text
//! Source-derived scalar layouts. Admission and work costs belong to sibling modules.
use crate::{Error, InputDecl, Program, Statement, Type, UInt};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Origin {
    Input,
    Let,
    Event,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct CaptureSlot {
    pub name: String,
    pub ty: Type,
    pub origin: Origin,
    pub ordinal: u16,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct StageBinder {
    pub name: String,
    pub ty: Type,
}
impl From<&InputDecl> for StageBinder {
    fn from(value: &InputDecl) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: value.name.clone(),
            ty: value.ty,
        }
    }
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct AwaitSite {
    pub site: u16,
    pub ordinal: u16,
    pub label: String,
    pub binders: Vec<StageBinder>,
    pub captures: Vec<CaptureSlot>,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct ActionPlan {
    pub action: String,
    pub statement_count: u16,
    pub sites: Vec<AwaitSite>,
    pub segment_cost: Vec<UInt>,
    pub committed_before: Vec<UInt>,
    pub plan_total: UInt,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct StagePlan {
    pub format: String,
    pub program_hash: String,
    pub actions: Vec<ActionPlan>,
}

/// Builds layouts after validate_v2. Costs and hashes are filled by stage::load.
pub(crate) fn build(program: &Program) -> Result<StagePlan, Error> {
    let mut actions = Vec::new();
    for action in &program.actions {
        let mut types: BTreeMap<_, _> = program
            .states
            .iter()
            .map(|state| (state.name.clone(), state.ty))
            .collect();
        let mut captures = Vec::new();
        for (ordinal, input) in action.inputs.iter().enumerate() {
            types.insert(input.name.clone(), input.ty);
            captures.push(CaptureSlot {
                name: input.name.clone(),
                ty: input.ty,
                origin: Origin::Input,
                ordinal: ordinal as u16,
            });
        }
        let mut sites = Vec::new();
        for (ordinal, statement) in action.statements.iter().enumerate() {
            match statement {
                Statement::Let { name, value } => {
                    let ty = crate::runtime::expr_type(program, *value, &types, 0)?;
                    types.insert(name.clone(), ty);
                    captures.push(CaptureSlot {
                        name: name.clone(),
                        ty,
                        origin: Origin::Let,
                        ordinal: ordinal as u16,
                    });
                }
                Statement::Await { label, binders, .. } => {
                    sites.push(AwaitSite {
                        site: sites.len() as u16 + 1,
                        ordinal: ordinal as u16,
                        label: label.clone(),
                        binders: binders.iter().map(StageBinder::from).collect(),
                        captures: captures.clone(),
                    });
                    for binder in binders {
                        types.insert(binder.name.clone(), binder.ty);
                        captures.push(CaptureSlot {
                            name: binder.name.clone(),
                            ty: binder.ty,
                            origin: Origin::Event,
                            ordinal: ordinal as u16,
                        });
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        actions.push(ActionPlan {
            action: action.name.clone(),
            statement_count: action.statements.len() as u16,
            sites,
            segment_cost: Vec::new(),
            committed_before: Vec::new(),
            plan_total: UInt(0),
        });
    }
    Ok(StagePlan {
        format: "moriarty-stage-plan/1".into(),
        program_hash: String::new(),
        actions,
    })
}
``````

``````text
//! Profile isolation between `moriarty-core/1` and `moriarty-core/2` consumers.
//! Both helpers keep the existing `mori::core::profile` error identity.
use super::{LANGUAGE_2, SEMANTICS_2};
use crate::{Error, LANGUAGE, Program, SEMANTICS, Statement};

const PROFILE_MESSAGE: &str = "Unsupported language or semantics identity.";

/// Required at every `/1` entry point before evaluation or layout. An
/// in-memory program labelled `/1` that still carries an Await is refused.
pub fn require_core1(program: &Program) -> Result<(), Error> {
    if program.language != LANGUAGE || program.semantics != SEMANTICS {
        return Err(Error::new("profile", PROFILE_MESSAGE));
    }
    if program
        .actions
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|action| &action.statements)
        .any(|statement| matches!(statement, Statement::Await { .. }))
    {
        return Err(Error::new("profile", "Await requires moriarty-core/2."));
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Required at every staged entry point; `/1` programs are refused.
pub fn require_core2(program: &Program) -> Result<(), Error> {
    if program.language != LANGUAGE_2 || program.semantics != SEMANTICS_2 {
        return Err(Error::new("profile", PROFILE_MESSAGE));
    }
    Ok(())
}
``````

``````text
//! Complete qualified JSON envelopes for the local Core/2 outcome API.
use super::{STAGE_LABELS, StageOutcome, StageRejection};
use serde_json::{Value, json};

/// Render an outcome or rejection without executing a program or performing I/O.
/// Every envelope retains the explicit local-stage qualifications.
pub fn outcome_report(result: Result<StageOutcome, StageRejection>) -> Value {
    let mut report = match result {
        Ok(StageOutcome::Waiting {
            advanced,
            segment,
            continuation,
            attempted,
            residual,
        }) => {
            let committed = continuation.logical.committed;
            json!({"status":"waiting","advanced":advanced,"segment":segment,
                "continuation":continuation,"attempted":attempted,
                "committed":committed,"residual":residual})
        }
        Ok(StageOutcome::Complete {
            segment,
            committed,
            attempted,
            residual,
        }) => json!({"status":"complete","segment":segment,"attempted":attempted,
                "committed":committed,"residual":residual}),
        Err(rejected) => json!({"status":"rejected","error":rejected.error,
            "attempted":rejected.attempted,"committed":rejected.committed}),
    };
    let object = report
        .as_object_mut()
        .expect("stage reports are JSON objects");
    for (name, value) in STAGE_LABELS {
        object.insert(name.into(), Value::String(value.into()));
    }
    report
}
``````

Original SHA256 d301530692f2f02a51bb68cf8b30ee51db6d3f3c9019b9045ed2a50e3ad8debf; exact 18486 bytes; aliases: ["context/crates/mori-core/src/stage/validate.rs"]

``````text
//! `/2` static validation and stage plan invariants.
//!
//! `validate_v2` applies every legacy `/1` program check with the legacy codes
//! and messages, plus the Await rules: top-level placement (structural in IR),
//! unique labels, non-shadowing binders, Bool guards typed over the prefix and
//! the Await's own binders, the per-action bounds, and `await`/`when` reserved.
//! Legacy `validate` is unchanged and remains `/1`-only.
use super::{
    AwaitSite, CaptureSlot, LANGUAGE_2, MAX_AWAITS_PER_ACTION, MAX_CAPTURE_SLOTS,
    MAX_EVENT_BINDERS, Origin, SEMANTICS_2, STAGE_PLAN_FORMAT, StageBinder, StagePlan,
};
use crate::runtime::{
    expr_type, identifier, require_uint, validate_asset, validate_liability_reads,
};
use crate::{
    Error, Expr, MAX_DECLARATIONS, MAX_EXPRESSIONS, MAX_STATEMENTS, Program, Statement, Type, UInt,
};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

fn failure(code: &str, message: impl Into<String>) -> Error {
    Error::new(code, message)
}

fn invariant(what: &str) -> Error {
    failure("program", format!("Stage plan invariant violated: {what}."))
}

/// Legacy identifier rule with `await` and `when` also reserved (C6).
fn identifier_v2(name: &str) -> bool {
    identifier(name) && !matches!(name, "await" | "when")
}

fn names_v2<'a>(values: impl Iterator<Item = &'a str>, kind: &str) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
    for name in values {
        if !identifier_v2(name) || !seen.insert(name) {
            return Err(failure(
                "duplicate",
                format!("Invalid or duplicate {kind} name {name:?}."),
            ));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Full finite validation of a `moriarty-core/2` program.
pub(crate) fn validate_v2(program: &Program) -> Result<(), Error> {
    if program.language != LANGUAGE_2 || program.semantics != SEMANTICS_2 {
        return Err(failure(
            "profile",
            "Unsupported language or semantics identity.",
        ));
    }
    if !identifier_v2(&program.name) {
        return Err(failure(
            "name",
            "Agreement name must be a non-reserved ASCII identifier of at most 64 bytes.",
        ));
    }
    if program.actions.is_empty() {
        return Err(failure("program", "Program needs at least one action."));
    }
    if program.states.len() + program.assets.len() + program.actions.len() > MAX_DECLARATIONS
        || program.expressions.len() > MAX_EXPRESSIONS
    {
        return Err(failure(
            "bound",
            "Program exceeds finite declaration/expression bounds.",
        ));
    }
    names_v2(
        program
            .states
            .iter()
            .map(|s| s.name.as_str())
            .chain(program.assets.iter().map(|a| a.name.as_str())),
        "declaration",
    )?;
    names_v2(program.actions.iter().map(|a| a.name.as_str()), "action")?;
    let mut identities = BTreeSet::new();
    for asset in &program.assets {
        let id = &asset.identity;
        if id.network.is_empty()
            || id.issuer.is_empty()
            || id.reference.is_empty()
            || id.network.len() > 1024
            || id.issuer.len() > 1024
            || id.reference.len() > 1024
            || id.scale > 38
            || !identities.insert(id)
        {
            return Err(failure(
                "asset",
                "Asset identities must be complete, unique and use scale 0..38.",
            ));
        }
        if program.assets.iter().any(|other| {
            other.identity.network == id.network
                && other.identity.issuer == id.issuer
                && other.identity.reference == id.reference
                && other.identity.scale != id.scale
        }) {
            return Err(failure(
                "asset",
                "Same asset identity cannot have conflicting scales.",
            ));
        }
    }
    let mut depths = Vec::with_capacity(program.expressions.len());
    for (i, e) in program.expressions.iter().enumerate() {
        let refs = match e {
            Expr::Binary { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![*lhs, *rhs],
            Expr::Not { value } => vec![*value],
            _ => vec![],
        };
        let mut depth = 0;
        for r in refs {
            if usize::from(r) >= i {
                return Err(failure(
                    "expression",
                    "Expression references must point to earlier nodes; cycles are forbidden.",
                ));
            }
            depth = depth.max(depths[usize::from(r)] + 1);
        }
        if depth > 64 {
            return Err(failure("bound", "Expression depth exceeds 64."));
        }
        depths.push(depth);
    }
    let state_types: BTreeMap<_, _> = program
        .states
        .iter()
        .map(|s| (s.name.clone(), s.ty))
        .collect();
    for state in &program.states {
        if state.initial.ty() != state.ty {
            return Err(failure(
                "type",
                format!("Initial state {:?} has wrong type.", state.name),
            ));
        }
    }
    for action in &program.actions {
        if action.inputs.len() > MAX_DECLARATIONS || action.statements.len() > MAX_STATEMENTS {
            return Err(failure(
                "bound",
                "Action exceeds input or statement bounds.",
            ));
        }
        names_v2(action.inputs.iter().map(|i| i.name.as_str()), "input")?;
        let mut env = state_types.clone();
        for input in &action.inputs {
            if env.insert(input.name.clone(), input.ty).is_some()
                || program.assets.iter().any(|a| a.name == input.name)
            {
                return Err(failure("duplicate", "Input cannot shadow a declaration."));
            }
        }
        let mut labels = BTreeSet::new();
        let mut awaits = 0_usize;
        // Inputs, lets and earlier binders: the captures of the next site.
        let mut captured = action.inputs.len();
        for statement in &action.statements {
            match statement {
                Statement::Await {
                    label,
                    binders,
                    guard,
                } => {
                    awaits += 1;
                    if awaits > MAX_AWAITS_PER_ACTION {
                        return Err(failure("bound", "Action exceeds 16 awaits."));
                    }
                    if binders.len() > MAX_EVENT_BINDERS {
                        return Err(failure("bound", "Await exceeds 16 event binders."));
                    }
                    if captured > MAX_CAPTURE_SLOTS {
                        return Err(failure("bound", "Await site exceeds 256 capture slots."));
                    }
                    if !identifier_v2(label) || !labels.insert(label.as_str()) {
                        return Err(failure(
                            "duplicate",
                            format!("Invalid or duplicate await label {label:?}."),
                        ));
                    }
                    for binder in binders {
                        if !identifier_v2(&binder.name)
                            || env.insert(binder.name.clone(), binder.ty).is_some()
                            || program.assets.iter().any(|a| a.name == binder.name)
                        {
                            return Err(failure(
                                "duplicate",
                                "Await binder cannot shadow an existing name.",
                            ));
                        }
                    }
                    if expr_type(program, *guard, &env, 0)? != Type::Bool {
                        return Err(failure("type", "Await guard must have type Bool."));
                    }
                    captured += binders.len();
                }
                Statement::Let { name, value } => {
                    let ty = expr_type(program, *value, &env, 0)?;
                    if !identifier_v2(name)
                        || env.insert(name.clone(), ty).is_some()
                        || program.assets.iter().any(|a| a.name == *name)
                    {
                        return Err(failure("duplicate", "let cannot shadow an existing name."));
                    }
                    captured += 1;
                }
                Statement::Requires { predicate } | Statement::Ensures { predicate } => {
                    if expr_type(program, *predicate, &env, 0)? != Type::Bool {
                        return Err(failure("type", "Predicate must have type Bool."));
                    }
                }
                Statement::Next { state, value } => {
                    let expected = state_types
                        .get(state)
                        .ok_or_else(|| failure("name", format!("Unknown state {state:?}.")))?;
                    if expr_type(program, *value, &env, 0)? != *expected {
                        return Err(failure("type", "State update has wrong type."));
                    }
                }
                Statement::Emit { name, value } => {
                    if name.is_empty() || name.len() > 1024 {
                        return Err(failure("name", "Event name must contain 1..1024 bytes."));
                    }
                    expr_type(program, *value, &env, 0)?;
                }
                Statement::Transfer {
                    asset,
                    from,
                    to,
                    amount,
                }
                | Statement::Fee {
                    asset,
                    from,
                    to,
                    amount,
                } => {
                    validate_asset(program, asset)?;
                    if from.is_empty() || to.is_empty() || from.len() > 1024 || to.len() > 1024 {
                        return Err(failure("account", "Account identities cannot be empty."));
                    }
                    require_uint(program, *amount, &env)?;
                }
                Statement::Liability {
                    name,
                    asset,
                    debtor,
                    creditor,
                    amount,
                } => {
                    validate_asset(program, asset)?;
                    if name.is_empty()
                        || debtor.is_empty()
                        || creditor.is_empty()
                        || name.len() > 1024
                        || debtor.len() > 1024
                        || creditor.len() > 1024
                    {
                        return Err(failure(
                            "liability",
                            "Liability identities cannot be empty.",
                        ));
                    }
                    require_uint(program, *amount, &env)?;
                }
                Statement::Discharge { name, amount } => {
                    if name.is_empty() || name.len() > 1024 {
                        return Err(failure(
                            "liability",
                            "Liability name must contain 1..1024 bytes.",
                        ));
                    }
                    require_uint(program, *amount, &env)?;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    validate_liability_reads(program)?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Independently re-derives each action's sites and capture layouts and
/// requires the Sol-built plan to equal them, then checks the A3 predicates
/// explicitly. Runs before costing, so cost vectors and hash must be empty.
pub(crate) fn plan_invariants(program: &Program, plan: &StagePlan) -> Result<(), Error> {
    if plan.format != STAGE_PLAN_FORMAT {
        return Err(invariant("format"));
    }
    if !plan.program_hash.is_empty() {
        return Err(invariant("program hash filled before costing"));
    }
    if plan.actions.len() != program.actions.len() {
        return Err(invariant("action count"));
    }
    let state_names: BTreeSet<_> = program.states.iter().map(|s| s.name.as_str()).collect();
    for (action, ap) in program.actions.iter().zip(&plan.actions) {
        if ap.action != action.name || usize::from(ap.statement_count) != action.statements.len() {
            return Err(invariant("action identity"));
        }
        if !ap.segment_cost.is_empty()
            || !ap.committed_before.is_empty()
            || ap.plan_total != UInt(0)
        {
            return Err(invariant("costs filled before costing"));
        }
        // Independent derivation in declaration and statement order.
        let mut types: BTreeMap<_, _> = program
            .states
            .iter()
            .map(|s| (s.name.clone(), s.ty))
            .collect();
        let mut slots = Vec::with_capacity(action.inputs.len());
        for (index, input) in action.inputs.iter().enumerate() {
            types.insert(input.name.clone(), input.ty);
            slots.push(CaptureSlot {
                name: input.name.clone(),
                ty: input.ty,
                origin: Origin::Input,
                ordinal: u16::try_from(index).map_err(|_| invariant("input ordinal"))?,
            });
        }
        let mut expected = Vec::new();
        for (index, statement) in action.statements.iter().enumerate() {
            let ordinal = u16::try_from(index).map_err(|_| invariant("statement ordinal"))?;
            match statement {
                Statement::Let { name, value } => {
                    let ty = expr_type(program, *value, &types, 0)?;
                    types.insert(name.clone(), ty);
                    slots.push(CaptureSlot {
                        name: name.clone(),
                        ty,
                        origin: Origin::Let,
                        ordinal,
                    });
                }
                Statement::Await { label, binders, .. } => {
                    expected.push(AwaitSite {
                        site: u16::try_from(expected.len() + 1).map_err(|_| invariant("site"))?,
                        ordinal,
                        label: label.clone(),
                        binders: binders.iter().map(StageBinder::from).collect(),
                        captures: slots.clone(),
                    });
                    for binder in binders {
                        types.insert(binder.name.clone(), binder.ty);
                        slots.push(CaptureSlot {
                            name: binder.name.clone(),
                            ty: binder.ty,
                            origin: Origin::Event,
                            ordinal,
                        });
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        if ap.sites != expected {
            return Err(invariant("sites differ from source"));
        }
        // Explicit A3 predicates, stated separately from the derivation.
        if ap.sites.len() > MAX_AWAITS_PER_ACTION {
            return Err(failure("bound", "Action exceeds 16 awaits."));
        }
        let mut previous: Option<&AwaitSite> = None;
        for (index, site) in ap.sites.iter().enumerate() {
            if usize::from(site.site) != index + 1 {
                return Err(invariant("sites are not numbered 1..N"));
            }
            if previous.is_some_and(|p| p.ordinal >= site.ordinal) {
                return Err(invariant("ordinals are not strictly increasing"));
            }
            if site.binders.len() > MAX_EVENT_BINDERS || site.captures.len() > MAX_CAPTURE_SLOTS {
                return Err(failure("bound", "Await site exceeds stage layout bounds."));
            }
            let inputs = action.inputs.len();
            if site.captures.len() < inputs
                || site.captures[..inputs]
                    .iter()
                    .zip(&action.inputs)
                    .enumerate()
                    .any(|(i, (slot, input))| {
                        slot.origin != Origin::Input
                            || slot.name != input.name
                            || slot.ty != input.ty
                            || usize::from(slot.ordinal) != i
                    })
            {
                return Err(invariant("captures do not begin with all inputs"));
            }
            let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
            for slot in &site.captures {
                if state_names.contains(slot.name.as_str())
                    || !seen.insert(slot.name.as_str())
                    || (slot.origin != Origin::Input && slot.ordinal >= site.ordinal)
                {
                    return Err(invariant(
                        "capture names a state, repeats or follows its site",
                    ));
                }
            }
            if let Some(p) = previous
                && !site.captures.starts_with(&p.captures)
            {
                return Err(invariant("captures are not prefix-monotone"));
            }
            previous = Some(site);
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Checks the filled cost vectors: N+1 entries, prefix sums, and a total that
/// also equals the per-statement sum plus one entry charge per await.
pub(crate) fn cost_invariants(program: &Program, plan: &StagePlan) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let overflow = || failure("bound", "Stage logical plan exceeds u128.");
    for (action, ap) in program.actions.iter().zip(&plan.actions) {
        let segments = ap.sites.len() + 1;
        if ap.segment_cost.len() != segments || ap.committed_before.len() != segments {
            return Err(invariant("cost vector lengths"));
        }
        let mut running = 0_u128;
        for (cost, before) in ap.segment_cost.iter().zip(&ap.committed_before) {
            if before.0 != running {
                return Err(invariant("committed_before is not a prefix sum"));
            }
            running = running.checked_add(cost.0).ok_or_else(overflow)?;
        }
        if ap.plan_total.0 != running {
            return Err(invariant("plan total"));
        }
        let mut independent = u128::try_from(ap.sites.len()).map_err(|_| overflow())?;
        for statement in &action.statements {
            let cost = super::cost::statement_cost(program, statement)?;
            independent = independent.checked_add(cost.0).ok_or_else(overflow)?;
        }
        if independent != running {
            return Err(invariant("plan total differs from statement costs"));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
``````

``````text
# Core continuations

`moriarty/2` adds typed suspension and resumption to Rust Core. An action can
return a local prefix and a continuation, then evaluate its remaining statements
when supplied a typed event. Existing `moriarty/1` programs retain their atomic
semantics, JSON and logical-cost profile.

Current selected evidence covers **88 distinct focused Rust test functions**:
17 functions passed in the last closure captures (12 public CLI and 5 Core
compatibility cases). Another 71 functions are retained on unchanged selected
call paths: 40 other Core, 15 backend normal/relation, 9 ledger closure/profile,
6 backend frame and 1 legacy byte-comparison case. This is not a fresh rerun of
all 88 functions. See

and [closure source scope](audits/2026-10-15/core-continuations/SOURCE-SCOPE-CLOSURE.json)

## Write an await

The [delivery example](../examples/core/continuations/delivery.mori) contains:

```mori
language "moriarty/2";
agreement ContinuationEscrowOracle {
  asset PAY = { network: "local", issuer: "continuation-escrow-oracle", reference: "PAY", scale: 0 };
  state marker: UInt = 77;
  action deliver(amount: UInt) {
    transfer(PAY, "alice", "escrow", amount);
    liability("release", PAY, "escrow", "bob", amount);
    await delivery(ready: Bool) when ready;
    transfer(PAY, "escrow", "bob", amount);
    discharge("release", amount);
  }
}
```

`delivery` names this await site. Its event declares a Bool named `ready`; the
guard has type Bool. Event binders may use Bool or UInt. Labels are unique within
an action, and binders cannot shadow existing names. The current bounds are
16 awaits per action, 16 event binders per site and 256 capture slots.

Reaching the await ends the current segment before evaluating its guard. With
the supplied scenario (`amount` = 10), the local prefix has balances `alice` 90,
`escrow` 10 and `bob` 0, plus a `release` duty of 10. The remaining transfer and
discharge have not run.
`requires` and `ensures` remain assertions at their source positions; a false
assertion does not become an await.

## Start and resume through the CLI

From the repository root, the start interface is:

```sh
mori simulate examples/core/continuations/delivery.mori \
  --action deliver \
  --scenario examples/core/continuations/delivery-scenario.json \
  --logical-cap 11
```

Save the result's **`continuation` member alone** as `continuation.json`.
Resume takes that object, not the full waiting report or a segment history.

```sh
mori simulate examples/core/continuations/delivery.mori \
  --resume continuation.json \
  --event examples/core/continuations/delivery-false-resume.json

mori simulate examples/core/continuations/delivery.mori \
  --resume continuation.json \
  --event examples/core/continuations/delivery-true-resume-complete.json
```

A false guard returns `status:"waiting"`, `advanced:false`, `segment:null` and
the unchanged continuation. It produces no new prefix. A true guard runs only
the remainder: the delivery example reaches balances `alice` 90, `escrow` 0 and
`bob` 10, and retains the `release` duty present with amount 0. Funding is not
repeated.

An event file supplies an ordered, named, typed tuple:

```json
{"format":"moriarty-stage-event/1","action":"deliver","label":"delivery","values":[{"name":"ready","value":{"type":"Bool","value":true}}]}
```

`--resume` requires `--event` and conflicts with `--scenario`, `--trace`,
`--target` and authorization arguments. An optional resume `--action` must
match the continuation. `--logical-cap` is optional on start and resume.
Waiting and complete results exit with status 0; rejected stages exit with
status 1. A rejected suffix
returns its error and attempted work, with no segment or replacement
continuation; the prior local prefix and input continuation remain available.

The stored `continuation.logical.cap` is outside both continuation digests,
`program_hash` and `plan_hash`. A caller can edit it, remove it or raise it,
and resume will not detect the change. Treat it as a local advisory ceiling.
It is not an authenticated lifetime work budget. Resume still checks that
`logical.committed` matches the planned prefix work for the stored `site`.
An optional resume `--logical-cap` must not exceed a present stored cap. The
effective cap, which is that flag when given and otherwise the stored cap,
must cover `committed` plus the next segment. None of these
checks authenticates the continuation or records its consumption.

Every staged JSON report and `/4` manifest carries the Opus-authored labels exactly:

```json
{"qualification":"local-reference-stage","authentication":"none","consumption":"untracked"}
```

The [Opus-authored stage contract](../crates/mori-core/src/stage/mod.rs) records
their scope. Consult the [security ownership record](audits/2026-10-14/SECURITY-ROUTING.md)
and the separately scoped [Opus security review](audits/2026-10-14/SECURITY-REVIEW.md)
for security analysis. This guide describes language and tool behavior.

## What survives a boundary

Action inputs and evaluated lets are captured by value. Earlier accepted event
binders are captured for later awaits. State and liabilities are read from the
current boundary. To retain a state value as it stood earlier, bind it explicitly,
for example `let savedBasis = basis;`.

The [two-await reserve example](../examples/core/continuations/reserve.mori)
starts with `basis` 40 and `extra` 2. It captures `held` 42, then updates `basis`
to 35. The accepted event value `quote` 43 remains available after the second
await; `basis` has meanwhile become 78. The final segment uses `held` 42 and
`quote` 43 rather than recomputing them from `basis` 78. Completion retains an
allocation duty of 5.

`residual` lists every positive liability in the post boundary. Completing an
action does not erase those duties or report settlement. Each awaiting action
has one pending frame in the staged representation; the local qualifications
above remain part of every result.

## Logical work and compilation

The profile is `moriarty-reference-logical-cost/2`. It counts statement dispatch
and distinct expression-node visits with a fresh cache per statement. A plan
records the successful cost of each segment. Reaching an await charges its entry;
resuming charges dispatch and evaluates the guard.

For delivery, start costs 5 and a true resume costs 6, for 11 committed units.
A false resume reports 2 attempted units while committed work remains 5. A later
true resume still completes at 11 committed units. Reserve has segment costs
11, 15 and 10, for 36 committed units. Attempted work on a false or rejected
invocation is reported separately.

These units are not circuit cost, DUST, service fees or proof measurements.
The unsigned compiler source path emits `/4` staged artifacts with `N + 1` circuits
for N awaits; a false observation has no circuit. Zero-await `/2` actions have
one circuit. The CLI compilation interface is:

```sh
mori compile examples/core/continuations/delivery.mori \
  --target target.json --out new-output-directory
```

The target is supplied separately. Staged manifests and ZKIR source retain their
unperformed qualification gates. The local CLI results above do not establish
native proof or target qualification.

## Rust API

Use [`mori_core::stage`](../crates/mori-core/src/stage/mod.rs):

```rust
let program = mori_core::stage::load(source)?;
let outcome = mori_core::stage::start(&program, "deliver", scenario, Some(mori_core::UInt(11)))?;
// Match StageOutcome::Waiting to obtain its Continuation.
let next = mori_core::stage::resume(&program, continuation, event, None, None)?;
```

`StagedProgram` exposes its parsed program and plan through read-only getters.
`StageOutcome` distinguishes Waiting and Complete; its segments include frame
pre/post values and an Execution with original source statement indices.
`StageRejection` contains error, attempted and committed work. Legacy `parse`,
`validate` and `simulate` remain `/1` entry points.
``````

``````text
# Normal Core/1 execution reports

This contract defines the adopted public report design for accepted finite Rust `language "moriarty/1"` / `moriarty-core/1` actions using `Let`, `Requires`, `Next`, `Ensures` and `Emit`, including an otherwise valid empty action. It defines their observations without changing source typing or arithmetic. Other financial statements retain their existing semantics and reports. Core/2 staged reports and target compilation have separate contracts.

Design adoption on 2026-10-18 establishes these requirements. Runtime behavior, source-to-IR correspondence and exact public bytes require separate conformance evidence; this document records no such result. The clauses refine existing [UNI-018/020/021/024](../openspec/changes/consolidated-language-kernel/specs/consolidated-language-kernel/spec.md#requirement-uni-018-profile-and-consumer-admission), with child labels NR-01–06.

## Public envelope and execution identity

For a successfully printed ordinary `mori simulate` result, the public envelope SHALL contain exactly `status: "accepted"`, `qualification: "local-reference-execution"` and `execution`. Execution SHALL contain exactly `semantics`, `action`, `pre`, `post`, `steps` and `effects`. Its semantics SHALL be `moriarty-core/1`, and its action SHALL be the selected action's name.

For an action with N statements, `steps` SHALL contain N entries in source order. Each Step SHALL contain all five members: `index`, `statement`, `value`, `snapshot` and `effects`. Entry i SHALL carry numeric zero-based `index: i` and the exact serialized statement i from the admitted public IR. Each ExprId in that statement SHALL be a numeric zero-based reference to the same Program's `expressions` array. An ExprId identifies an expression, rather than its evaluated value, source offset or Step. Numbering belongs to the exact source/IR candidate; it is not promised to survive source edits. These are NR-01 identity requirements.

Under NR-02, every accepted statement of the five scoped kinds SHALL have a present typed outer `Step.value`. UInt uses a canonical decimal string, for example `{"type":"UInt","value":"7"}`. Bool uses a JSON boolean, for example `{"type":"Bool","value":true}`. The outer Option encodes Some as that typed object and None as JSON null; null or an omitted outer `value` is not the selected representation for these completed statement kinds. This reporting rule does not change input decoding elsewhere.

`statement.value`, where present, is an ExprId number. The outer `Step.value` is the typed evaluation result. For example, `Let { name: "total", value: 2 }` can report outer `value: {"type":"UInt","value":"7"}`. The reference 2 and result 7 have different meanings.

## Sequential values and complete snapshots

Let S[-1] be `execution.pre` and S[i] the complete snapshot after statement i. A Snapshot SHALL contain exactly `state`, `balances` and `liabilities`. It SHALL retain affected and preserved rows, with declared state names mapped to typed values, balances ordered by exact `(asset, account)` and liabilities ordered by name. Asset comparison uses `(network, issuer, reference, scale)`. Inputs and local let captures are not Snapshot state fields.

NR-03 requires `pre` to be the complete normalized starting snapshot, including declared initial values selected by an empty supplied state map. Each `steps[i].snapshot` SHALL equal S[i]. For N>0, `post` SHALL equal the final Step snapshot. A let capture remains available to later statements while retaining its captured value; `Next` updates state immediately for subsequent expressions.

Define Eval(e,i) as the typed semantic value of expression e immediately before statement i, using the then-current state, action inputs and earlier captures. This notation specifies evaluation; it is not a call to an implementation.

| Statement | Required outer Step.value | Complete snapshot after statement | New Step.effects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Let { name, value: e }` | Eval(e,i), captured under name | S[i-1] | `[]` |
| `Requires { predicate: e }` | typed Bool true | S[i-1] | `[]` |
| `Next { state: x, value: e }` | after = Eval(e,i), evaluated before assigning x | S[i-1] with only x replaced by after | exactly `[State { name: x, before: S[i-1].state[x], after }]` |
| `Ensures { predicate: e }` | typed Bool true, at its written position | S[i-1] | `[]` |
| `Emit { name, value: e }` | v = Eval(e,i) | S[i-1] | exactly `[Emit { name, value: v }]` |

The typed Let capture is observable even though its snapshot and effects do not change. `Ensures` reads the state at its own source position. Emit records an event while preserving the snapshot.

NR-04 defines `Step.effects` as the ordered effects newly produced by that statement. Define P[-1]=[] and P[i] as P[i-1] followed by `steps[i].effects`. `execution.effects` SHALL equal the ordered concatenation of all Step deltas, preserving repeated effects and array order. P is a derived prefix, not another wire field. Final state alone cannot supply this effect history, and unchanged snapshots can accompany Emit effects.

For N=0, `steps` SHALL be `[]`, `post` SHALL equal the complete normalized `pre`, and `effects` SHALL be `[]`, the empty concatenation P[-1]. Semantics and selected action identity remain present. No synthetic Step, statement index, ExprId or Step.value is created; per-Step rules have no instance for an empty action.

## Complete Counter illustration and logical work

The following exact specimen illustrates the adopted requirements with input amount UInt7 and empty supplied state, balances and liabilities:

```mori
language "moriarty/1";
agreement Counter {
  state count: UInt = 0;
  action run(amount: UInt) {
    let total = count + amount;
    requires total <= 100;
    next count = total;
    ensures count == total;
    emit "count"(count);
  }
}
```

Its public expression table has the following source-grounded numbering. The declared initial value is a StateDecl literal, not an action expression node. Independent correspondence to an actual parsed Program remains a separate compared observation.

| ExprId | Expression |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Name count in Let |
| 1 | Name amount |
| 2 | Add(0,1) |
| 3 | Name total in Requires |
| 4 | Literal UInt100 |
| 5 | Le(3,4) |
| 6 | Name total in Next |
| 7 | Name count in Ensures |
| 8 | Name total in Ensures |
| 9 | Eq(7,8) |
| 10 | Name count in Emit |

Here UInt7 and Bool true abbreviate the typed objects above. S0 is `{state:{count:UInt0},balances:[],liabilities:[]}`; S7 differs only by count UInt7. C is `State { name: "count", before: UInt0, after: UInt7 }`, and E is `Emit { name: "count", value: UInt7 }`.

| index | Exact statement fields | Step.value | snapshot | Step.effects | Derived P[i] | Logical units |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `kind:Let,name:total,value:2` | UInt7 | S0 | [] | [] | 4 |
| 1 | `kind:Requires,predicate:5` | Bool true | S0 | [] | [] | 4 |
| 2 | `kind:Next,state:count,value:6` | UInt7 | S7 | [C] | [C] | 2 |
| 3 | `kind:Ensures,predicate:9` | Bool true | S7 | [] | [C] | 4 |
| 4 | `kind:Emit,name:count,value:10` | UInt7 | S7 | [E] | [C,E] | 2 |

Thus `pre` is S0, `post` is S7 and `execution.effects` is [C,E]. Neither total nor amount becomes a state field. Under the existing `moriarty-reference-logical-cost/1` schedule, each dispatched statement and each uncached expression node costs one logical unit, with a fresh cache per statement. The five increments are `1+3`, `1+3`, `1+1`, `1+3`, `1+1`, totaling16. They describe reference interpretation, not fees or target execution, and introduce no per-Step cost field.

NR-05 requires a positive metered invocation with a sufficient cap to retain exactly the same complete Execution as the corresponding unmetered invocation. Its public envelope SHALL retain status and qualification, adding only `profile: "moriarty-reference-logical-cost/1"` and `logical: { cap, used }`, with canonical decimal strings. For this Counter at cap16, cap SHALL be `"16"` and used SHALL be `"16"`. The example and arithmetic are requirements, not generated goldens or observed executions.

## Public serialization and existing compatibility

NR-06 requires a successfully printed normal accepted result, ordinary or metered, to return exit0 and print one complete JSON report followed by one final newline, with no ordinary status text on stderr. The existing bounded pretty public exporter is retained. Complete semantic JSON equality and independently frozen public-byte compatibility SHALL be checked separately. Object member order is not execution semantics; statement, effect and snapshot-row arrays retain their prescribed ordering. Exact bytes must not be inferred from library field declaration order.

The existing [normal Transfer oracle](../crates/mori/tests/core_test_report.rs) uses the original `mori test` aggregate/report consumer. Its complete accepted-case Execution, under `cases[].actual.Ok`, and original aggregate bytes SHALL remain unchanged. The legacy small-report byte pin is for that 28,093-byte `mori test` aggregate; it is not a byte golden for the ordinary three-field `mori simulate` accepted envelope. Its Requires predicate2 reports Bool true with the pre snapshot and no effects. Its Transfer amount-expression3 reports UInt25 with the complete post snapshot and one new Transfer effect; Execution.effects is the same one-element ordered list. Exact TEST identity is `(local, independent-report-oracle, TEST, scale0)`. Alice100/bob0 becomes alice75/bob25; sixteen observer balances42, incoming_duty11 and empty state remain preserved. The five-kind table does not redefine Transfer's own semantics. This example's single final effect and lack of Let cannot independently establish the new Let result or distinguish delta from prefix reporting. Counter and empty-action `simulate` envelopes require their own independently frozen public-byte expectations.

## Adopted financial observation extension

This section defines the adopted additive observation contract for normally accepted finite Rust `moriarty/1` / `moriarty-core/1` Transfer, Fee, Liability and Discharge statements. Its SHALL clauses are effective design requirements under the [recorded design adoption](../evidence/utxo/doctorwatson-language-loop-2026-10-17/financial-report-adoption-20261018/DESIGN-ADOPTION.json) of 2026-10-18. They do not replace NR-01–06, broaden the earlier five-kind adoption, or change typing, arithmetic, admission or financial transitions. The author inspected implementation source; this design is not independent behavior proof, a golden or an executed result. Core/2, other language profiles and target consumers retain separate contracts.

Current Core/1 has no Mint, Burn or dedicated accrual statement. Liability creates a named duty or adds an explicitly supplied amount. This addition supplies no interest rate, time basis, day-count, compounding or accrual schedule. Mint/burn and dedicated accrual remain missing language/financial obligations where required by the broader product; this report extension neither implements nor removes them.

Let S[-1] be the complete normalized Execution.pre and S[i] the complete snapshot immediately after statement i. Let q be the UInt result of that statement's amount expression evaluated immediately before its transition, using current state, action inputs, earlier captures and current liability reads under existing Core semantics. For Transfer, Fee and Liability, let A be the exact declared AssetId denoted by the statement's asset alias. Discharge uses the existing duty row's AssetId, debtor and creditor in S[i-1]. For each completed financial statement, the Step SHALL have exactly index, statement, value, snapshot and effects. The numeric zero-based index SHALL be its ordinal in the selected action, including preceding nonfinancial statements. The exact admitted statement SHALL retain these members in addition to kind:

| kind | Statement members | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Transfer | asset, from, to, amount | asset alias, account strings, amount ExprId |
| Fee | asset, from, to, amount | asset alias, account strings, amount ExprId |
| Liability | name, asset, debtor, creditor, amount | duty name, asset alias, party strings, amount ExprId |
| Discharge | name, amount | existing duty name, amount ExprId |

Statement.amount SHALL remain the numeric zero-based reference into that Program's expressions array. The outer Step.value SHALL instead contain the present typed UInt object with type "UInt" and value q's canonical unsigned decimal string, including zero. It SHALL report the moved, charged, added or discharged amount, respectively; neither the ExprId, a boolean success value, recipient balance nor closing duty amount shall replace it. Null or omission SHALL NOT replace the typed object for a completed statement of these kinds. The following table defines the report projection of existing accepted transitions; it creates no new admission premise:

| Statement | Complete post-statement snapshot relative to S[i-1] | Exact new Step.effects |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Transfer | Existing movement of q in A between the two explicit account rows; preserve all other balances, state and liabilities | one Transfer {asset:A,from,to,amount:q} |
| Fee | Existing movement of q in A between the two explicit account rows; preserve all other balances, state and liabilities | one Fee {asset:A,from,to,amount:q} |
| Liability, row absent | Insert the identified duty with amount q in name order; preserve all other duties, balances and state | one Liability {name,asset:A,debtor,creditor,before:0,after:q} |
| Liability, row present with amount b | Preserve duty identity; replace only its amount with the existing checked sum b+q; preserve other duties, balances and state | one Liability {name,asset:A,debtor,creditor,before:b,after:b+q} |
| Discharge, row present with amount b | Preserve duty identity; replace only its amount with the existing checked difference b-q, retaining zero; preserve other duties, balances and state | one Liability {name,asset:existing asset,debtor:existing debtor,creditor:existing creditor,before:b,after:b-q} |

The brace forms denote exact effect field sets plus kind carrying the named variant. Each effect AssetId SHALL contain network, issuer, reference and scale, rather than the statement asset alias. Effect amount, before and after SHALL be canonical decimal strings without a typed Value wrapper. Discharge SHALL use the Liability effect variant; no new Discharge effect is introduced. The exact statement and complete prior snapshot SHALL retain the distinction among creation, addition and discharge. A Liability effect with before zero alone cannot distinguish absent creation from a present-zero opening duty.

For an already admitted self-transfer or self-fee, the numeric balance SHALL remain unchanged while the amount effect remains present. For an already admitted zero amount, the effect SHALL remain present even where numeric amounts do not change. Zero-amount Liability creation SHALL insert a present-zero duty; zero or full Discharge SHALL retain the existing duty row. These clauses add no admission authority. Discharge SHALL remain a duty reduction; any payment is a separate statement and Step.

Each Step.snapshot SHALL equal S[i] in full, containing exactly state, balances and liabilities. State SHALL retain all declared names and typed values; inputs and let captures SHALL NOT become state fields. Balance rows SHALL retain exactly account, full asset and amount; liability rows exactly name, full asset, debtor, creditor and amount. Affected and preserved rows, including observer balances and incoming duties admitted by Core, SHALL remain present. Balances SHALL be ordered by exact (asset,account), AssetId by (network,issuer,reference,scale), and liabilities by name. Absent and present-zero liabilities SHALL remain distinct. Empty state SHALL be {}, and empty balance/liability collections SHALL be [], not omitted or null. This frame concerns the admitted local snapshot and supplies no authenticated-domain or ledger-acceptance claim.

Step.effects SHALL contain only the statement's new effect, rather than an accumulated prefix. With P[-1]=[] and P[i]=P[i-1] followed by Step[i].effects, Execution.effects SHALL equal the ordered concatenation of all statement deltas, including intervening nonfinancial effects, preserving duplicates and zero/self effects. P remains derived notation, not a wire field. Complete snapshots and effect histories SHALL both be retained; unchanged numeric state does not imply empty effects. For N>0, post SHALL equal the last Step.snapshot. For N=0, the existing complete pre=post, steps:[] and effects:[] requirements remain, without a synthetic Step. Existing Execution/envelope fields and logical-work schedule remain unchanged; no per-Step work member is introduced. Any claimed ordinary/metered agreement SHALL compare the same complete Execution and independently specified work under the existing schedule.

Design adoption, source/IR correspondence, independent expectations, actual runtime observations and acceptance SHALL remain separate. Expectations for complete statements/ExprIds, typed values, snapshots, deltas, prefixes, work and consumer-specific bytes SHALL be independently derived and frozen before authorized runs, without generating them from the implementation under comparison. Existing financial-pair coverage and the normal Transfer aggregate compatibility case SHALL retain their exact scope; no full raw Step.value/statement or ordinary simulate-byte coverage is inferred. Original proposals, freezes, failures, five-kind adoption and pending normal-report cases SHALL remain unchanged. All U0–U7, M1–M17, MC/SP/G, full finance, ACTUS/DeFi and composition obligations remain. This observation contract decides no conservation, soundness, authorization, authentication, proof or security condition and supplies no hostile/security tests; those remain with the designated security owner. Internal review records remain separate from permissionless developer use.

## Provenance and conformance

The adopted design retains the original unadopted proposal and its review history. Its author had inspected implementation source; that exposure is disclosed and supplies no independent behavior proof. A separate custodian must derive and freeze complete expected inputs, IR, typed results, snapshots, deltas, prefixes, work and public bytes before a conformance run, without using the implementation under comparison to generate expectations. Original freezes and failures remain unchanged.

Implementation, source inspection, actual observations and acceptance remain separate for the exact profile, candidate and consumer under UNI-021. This report contract does not close a parent roadmap exit or broaden an existing financial, staged or target result. Public developers remain subject to the [permissionless product contract](MORIARTY-PRODUCT-CONTRACT.md); internal review and evidence records are not prerequisites for using the language.
``````
